publicPrompt:
Repair Emittery async iterator fanout and lifecycle. The full pinned repository lives in src/, including upstream docs and tests. This fixture contains explicitly injected production defects; it is not a claim about an upstream release. Edit only src/index.js. The package has no runtime dependencies. Use Node native tests, without installing dependencies or executing package scripts. Run node --test tests/visible.test.mjs from this workspace. Existing upstream tests need development dependencies and are source context only. Passing visible tests is a regression floor; implement every requirement below. Iterator delivery in this task concerns emit(), not emitSerial(); emitSerial() retains its existing ordinary listener behavior. Concurrent next() calls on the same iterator are outside this contract.

I-R1: Every emit(name, data) delivers one item to every currently registered events(name) iterator and every anyEvent() iterator independently. events([names]) subscribes to each listed name. Each iterator owns its FIFO backlog, so a fast consumer cannot consume or prevent delivery to a slower one. events() yields the data; anyEvent() yields [name, data]. Promise-valued data is awaited before yielding, and string, symbol and numeric event names keep their identity.

I-R2: Calling return() on an iterator unregisters only that iterator from all of its subscriptions, discards its own buffered items, makes its next() calls finish with {done:true}, and wakes a pending next() with that same done result. return() without an argument resolves to {done:true}; with an argument it resolves to {done:true,value:await argument}. Repeated return() calls must not affect any other old or newly created iterator.

I-R3: clearListeners(name) or clearListeners([names]) finishes and unregisters the iterators subscribed to the selected names. clearListeners() finishes/unregisters every named and any-event iterator. A finished iterator must yield all previously buffered items in order before returning {done:true}; if its backlog is empty, a pending next() must promptly resolve done. After its backlog drains, further next() calls remain done.

I-R4: Clearing a named channel leaves iterators on unrelated named channels and anyEvent() iterators active. Finishing or returning one iterator must preserve the registration and delivery of siblings, even when it subscribed to multiple names. New iterators created after an earlier iterator was cleared or returned work normally. Separate Emittery instances never share registrations, buffers or lifecycle effects.

I-R5: listenerCount(name) includes active named iterator subscriptions on that name and active anyEvent() iterators; listenerCount() includes every currently registered iterator subscription, so a multi-name iterator contributes one per subscribed name. Counts must update synchronously when an iterator is returned or cleared, without counting a finished iterator merely because it still has buffered data.

I-R6: Preserve ordinary on()/off() and once() behavior, including unsubscribe disposal, payload forwarding, and ordinary listeners called through emitSerial(). Iterators remain consumable with the standard next()/return() async iterator protocol.
